summary: Flame in Freefall is an offline-ready, multi-modal AI analytics and RAG platform that unifies 19 NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion investigations (748+ RAG chunks and 299+ VLM-analyzed flame frames). It addresses the challenge of fragmented spacecraft fire data by automatically extracting reports, tables, and flame imagery, normalizing all metrics into strict SI units (kPa, % O2, mm/s), and indexing them via FAISS with dynamic physics weighting and a local Qwen3-8B reasoning engine. In microgravity (0g) and lunar partial gravity (0.16g), flames behave unpredictably—forming invisible cool flames and spreading faster under low ventilation. Engineered to run 100% offline without internet dependency, our system empowers astronauts and aerospace engineers during deep-space communication blackouts to instantly compare flammability limits, smoke-vs-lunar-dust detection thresholds, and fire suppression protocols across ISS, Lunar Base, and Spacesuit environments.
details:
What it does & How it works:Flame in Freefall is a multi-modal AI analytics and RAG system that unifies 19 NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion investigations (748+ RAG chunks and 299+ VLM-analyzed flame frames) through a 5-stage pipeline. It extracts unstructured PDFs, experimental spreadsheets, and flame imagery, normalizes all metrics into strict SI units (kPa, % O2, mm/s), indexes them via FAISS with dynamic multi-factor weighting, and uses a local Qwen3-8B physics engine to synthesize cited fire-safety mechanisms.

Benefits & Intended Impact (Including Zero-Internet Deep-Space Readiness): Spacecraft fire behavior in microgravity (0g) and lunar partial gravity (0.16g) differs drastically from Earth due to the absence of buoyancy convection and the presence of invisible cool flames.

  • 100% Offline & Air-Gapped Spacecraft Operation: Engineered to run entirely offline on onboard laptops/workstations without any internet or cloud API dependency. During deep-space missions (Artemis Lunar Gateway, Moon bases, or Mars transit) where Earth communication suffers from severe latency (up to 20+ minutes) or total signal blackout, astronauts and mission specialists have immediate, autonomous access to AI fire-safety diagnostics and emergency suppression protocols.
  • Instant Multi-Environment Benchmarking: Allows engineers to instantly query, rank, and compare material flammability limits, ventilation thresholds, and smoke-vs-lunar-dust detection boundaries across ISS (101.35 kPa), Lunar Base (70.33 kPa), and Spacesuit (29.65 kPa) environments.

Tools, Languages & Stack:

  • Languages & Backend: Python, SQL, FastAPI, Uvicorn, SQLite, Pandas.
  • Local AI & Retrieval (Zero Cloud Dependency): bge-small-en-v1.5 (ONNX Runtime), local FAISS Vector Index, quantized Vision-Language Model (VLM), and local Qwen3-8B (llama.cpp server).
  • Frontend & Connectivity: Google AI Studio (React, Tailwind CSS, Recharts), Streamlit (offline local UI), Cloudflare Tunnel.

Creativity & Team Considerations:

  • Dynamic Physics-Weighted Retrieval: Combines semantic similarity with target habitat atmosphere matching (w_env_target), safety pillar filtering (Prevention, Detection, Suppression, Partial-G), and quantitative data density (w_quantitative).
  • Bilingual & Zero-Hallucination Design: Features an automated Vietnamese-to-English NASA terminology translation layer, strict SI unit conversion (psi to kPa, cm/s to mm/s), and mandatory [PSI-ID] source citations while running smoothly on consumer-grade hardware (24 GB RAM).
